title.zh: 卷六十六 唐書42: 列傳18 安重誨 朱弘昭 朱洪實 康義誠 藥彥稠 宋令詢
title.en: Volume 66 Book of Later Tang 42: Biographies 8: an Zhonghui, Zhu Hongzhao, Zhu Hongshi, Kang Yicheng, Yao Yanchou, Song Lingxun
title.raw: 卷六十六 唐書42: 列傳18 安重誨 朱弘昭 朱洪實 康義誠 藥彥稠 宋令詢 Volume 66 Book of Later Tang 42: Biographies 8: an Zhonghui, Zhu Hongzhao, Zhu Hongshi, Kang Yicheng, Yao Yanchou, Song Lingxun

sentences.zh: 安重誨，其先本北部豪長。

translations.literal: An Chonghui—his ancestors were originally great chiefs of the northern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui came from a line of great chiefs among the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 父福遷，為河東將，救兗、鄆而沒。

translations.literal: His father Fuqian served as a Hedong general and died while rescuing Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fuqian was a Hedong general who perished in the relief of Yan and Yun.

sentences.zh: 重誨自明宗龍潛時得給事左右。

translations.literal: Chonghui came to attend at the ruler's side from the time when Mingzong was still heir-apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui had served at Mingzong's side since before he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 及鎮邢州，以重誨為中門使。

translations.literal: When he took charge of Xingzhou, Chonghui was made Central Gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong held Xingzhou, he appointed Chonghui Central Gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 隨從征討，凡十餘年，委信無間，勤勞亦至。

translations.literal: Following him on campaigns for more than ten years, trust was never interrupted, and his labor reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he followed Mingzong on campaign; trust never wavered, and his exertions were beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 洎鄴城之變，佐命之功，獨居其右。

translations.literal: When the Ye city affair came, his merit in assisting the mandate stood alone at the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ye city crisis, his service in securing the throne stood above all others.

sentences.zh: 明宗踐祚，領樞密使，俄遷左領軍衛大將軍充職。

translations.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he headed the Privy Council; soon he was transferred to Left Army Guard senior general while retaining the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Chonghui headed the Privy Council and soon also held the post of senior general of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The text below is lost.)〉

sentences.zh: 明宗遣回鶻侯三馳傳至其國，侯三至醴泉縣，地素僻，無驛馬，縣令劉知章出獵，不時給馬，侯三遽以聞。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San on express relay to his country; when Hou reached Liquan County, the place was by nature remote and had no relay horses; magistrate Liu Zhizhang had gone hunting and did not supply horses in time; Hou San immediately reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San post-haste to his homeland. At remote Liquan County there were no relay mounts; the magistrate Liu Zhizhang was out hunting and failed to provide horses promptly, and Hou San reported the delay at once.

sentences.zh: 明宗大怒，械知章至京師，將殺之；

translations.literal: Mingzong was greatly angered, had Zhizhang shackled and brought to the capital, and was about to execute him;
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong flew into a rage, had Zhizhang shackled and sent to the capital, and meant to put him to death;

sentences.zh: 重誨從容為言，乃得不死。

translations.literal: Chonghui spoke calmly on his behalf, and he thus escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui pleaded for him calmly, and Zhizhang was spared.

sentences.zh: 明宗幸汴州，重誨建議欲因以伐吳，而明宗難之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong visited Bianzhou, Chonghui proposed taking the opportunity to attack Wu, but Mingzong found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Bianzhou, Chonghui urged using the occasion to strike Wu, but Mingzong hesitated.

sentences.zh: 其後，戶部尚書李鏻吳諜者言：「徐知誥欲奉吳國以稱藩，願得安公一言以為信。」

translations.literal: Later, Minister of Revenue Li Lin, through a Wu spy, said: "Xu Zhigao wishes to offer Wu as a vassal state and seeks one word from Lord An as pledge."
translations.idiomatic: Later Minister of Revenue Li Lin relayed a Wu spy's message: "Xu Zhigao wishes to submit Wu as a tributary state and asks for Lord An's word as assurance."

sentences.zh: 鏻即引諜者見重誨。

translations.literal: Lin immediately led the spy to see Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin at once brought the spy before Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 重誨大喜，以為然，乃以玉帶與諜者，使遺知誥為信，其直千緡。

translations.literal: Chonghui was greatly pleased, believed it true, and gave the spy a jade belt to send to Zhigao as pledge; it was worth a thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui was delighted, took it for truth, and gave the spy a jade belt to carry to Zhigao as token—worth a thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 重誨為樞密使，四五年間，獨綰大任，臧否自若，環衛、酋長、貴戚、近習，無敢幹政者。

translations.literal: As Privy Council commissioner for four or five years, he alone held great power; praise and blame were as he willed; guards, tribal chiefs, noble kin, and close attendants—none dared interfere in government.
translations.idiomatic: For four or five years as Privy Council commissioner he held power alone; none among the guards, tribal leaders, imperial kin, or inner circle dared meddle in affairs.

sentences.zh: 弟牧鄭州，子鎮懷、孟，身為中令，任過其才，議者謂必有覆餗之禍。

translations.literal: His younger brother held Zhengzhou, his sons held Huai and Meng, and he himself was chief councilor; his duties exceeded his talent, and observers said he would surely meet a disastrous fall.
translations.idiomatic: His brother governed Zhengzhou, his sons held Huai and Meng, and he was chief councilor himself—responsibilities beyond his gifts; many said ruin was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 無何，有吏人李虔徽弟揚言於眾云：「聞相者言其貴不可言，今將統軍征淮南。」

translations.literal: Before long a clerk, Li Qianhui's younger brother, proclaimed among the crowd: "I have heard a physiognomist say his nobility is beyond words; he will now command the army to campaign against Huainan."
translations.idiomatic: Soon a clerk, younger brother of Li Qianhui, declared in public: "I hear a fortune-teller say his rank is beyond telling—he is about to lead troops against Huainan."

sentences.zh: 時有軍將密以是聞，頗駭上聽。

translations.literal: At the time a military officer secretly reported this to the throne, which greatly alarmed the emperor's ear.
translations.idiomatic: A military officer secretly reported this, and it greatly troubled the emperor.

sentences.zh: 明宗謂重誨曰：「聞卿樹心腹，私市兵仗，欲自討淮南，有之否？」

translations.literal: Mingzong said to Chonghui, "I hear you have planted confidants and privately bought arms and armor, intending to campaign against Huainan yourself—is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong told Chonghui, "I hear you have gathered partisans and bought weapons on the sly, planning to take Huainan yourself—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 重誨惶恐，奏曰：「興師命將，出自宸衷，必是奸人結構，臣願陛下窮詰所言者。」

translations.literal: Chonghui was terrified and memorialized, "Dispatching armies and appointing commanders comes from the imperial mind; this must be villains' fabrication—I beg Your Majesty to interrogate fully whoever spoke thus."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui, in alarm, replied, "Only Your Majesty orders campaigns and commanders; this must be schemers' work—I beg you to trace whoever said it."

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝召侍衛指揮使安從進、藥彥稠等，謂之曰：「有人告安重誨私置兵仗，將不利於社稷，其若之何？」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor summoned Palace Guard commander An Congjin, Yao Yanchou, and others, and said to them, "Someone reports that An Chonghui has privately stored arms and intends harm to the altars of state—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Next day the emperor called An Congjin, Yao Yanchou, and others and asked, "Someone accuses An Chonghui of hoarding arms to harm the realm—what shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 從進等奏曰：「此是奸人結構，離間陛下勳舊。

translations.literal: Congjin and the rest memorialized, "This is villains' fabrication, driving a wedge between Your Majesty and your old merit.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "This is schemers' slander, meant to part Your Majesty from a loyal veteran.

sentences.zh: 且重誨事陛下三十年，從微至著，無不盡心，今日何苦乃圖不軌！

translations.literal: Moreover Chonghui has served Your Majesty thirty years, from obscurity to eminence, never failing in devotion—why should he now plot rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui has served you thirty years, rising from nothing, never stinting loyalty—why would he rebel now!

sentences.zh: 臣等以家屬保明，必無此事。」

translations.literal: We pledge our households in guarantee—there is surely no such matter."
translations.idiomatic: We stake our families on it—there is no such thing."

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's suspicions eased.

sentences.zh: 重誨三上表乞解機務，詔不允。

translations.literal: Chonghui thrice submitted memorials begging to be relieved of state affairs; the edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui three times asked to leave office; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 復麵奏：「乞與臣一鎮，以息謗議。」

translations.literal: He again addressed the throne in person: "I beg one circuit for your servant to quiet slander."
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded again in audience: "Grant me a post in one circuit to still the talk."

sentences.zh: 明宗不悅。

translations.literal: Mingzong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was annoyed.

sentences.zh: 重誨奏不已，明宗怒，謂曰：「放卿出，朕自有人！」

translations.literal: Chonghui memorialized without cease; Mingzong grew angry and said, "I release you—I have others!"
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui kept petitioning until Mingzong snapped, "Go then—I have others!"

sentences.zh: 即令武德使孟漢瓊至中書，與宰臣商量重誨事。

translations.literal: He at once ordered Martial Virtue commissioner Meng Hanqiong to the Secretariat to consult the chief ministers on Chonghui's affair.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Martial Virtue commissioner Meng Hanqiong to the Secretariat to discuss Chonghui with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 馮道言曰：「諸人苟惜安令公，解樞務為便。」

translations.literal: Feng Dao said, "If all wish to spare Lord An, relieving him of the Privy Council would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "If you mean to spare Lord An, let him leave the Privy Council."

sentences.zh: 趙鳳曰：「大臣豈可輕動，公失言也。」

translations.literal: Zhao Feng said, "A great minister must not be lightly moved—my lord has misspoken."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng said, "Great ministers must not be shifted lightly—you misspeak, sir."

sentences.zh: 道等因附漢瓊奏曰：「此斷自宸旨，然重臣不可輕議移改。」

translations.literal: Dao and the rest therefore added to Hanqiong's memorial, "This decision rests with the imperial mind, yet a great minister must not be lightly discussed for transfer."
translations.idiomatic: They told Hanqiong to report, "The decision is yours, Majesty, but do not lightly move a great minister."

sentences.zh: 由是兼命範延光為樞密使，重誨如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fan Yanguang was also appointed Privy Council commissioner, and Chonghui remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang was then made co-commissioner; Chonghui kept his post.

sentences.zh: 時以東川帥董璋恃險難製，乃以武虔裕為綿州刺史，董璋益懷疑忌，遂縶虔裕以叛。

translations.literal: At the time Eastern Chuan commander Dong Zhang relied on rugged terrain and was hard to control; Wuyou Yu was made Mianzhou prefect, and Zhang grew more suspicious, then imprisoned Yu and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Chuan's Dong Zhang held difficult country and defied control; when Wuyou Yu was sent to Mianzhou, Zhang's suspicions deepened and he imprisoned Yu and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 及石敬瑭領王師伐蜀，峽路艱阻，糧運不繼，明宗憂之，而重誨請行。

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang led the imperial army to conquer Shu, the gorge routes were arduous and grain could not follow; Mingzong worried, and Chonghui asked to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang's expedition into Shu stalled on bad passes and broken supply lines; Mingzong worried, and Chonghui volunteered to go west.

sentences.zh: 翌日，領數騎而出，日馳數百里，西諸侯聞之，莫不惶駭。

translations.literal: The next day he led several horsemen and set out, galloping several hundred li a day; western lords hearing of it were all terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he rode out with a few escorts, covering hundreds of li a day; western governors were terrified.

sentences.zh: 所在錢帛糧料，星夜輦運，人乘斃踣於山路者不可勝紀，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed, cash, silk, and grain were transported by night; men and horses collapsed dead on mountain roads beyond counting, and the people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Cash, grain, and fodder were rushed by night wherever he went; men and horses littered the roads dead beyond count, and the people groaned under it.

sentences.zh: 重誨至鳳翔，節度使朱弘昭延於寢室，令妻子奉食器，敬事尤謹。

translations.literal: When Chonghui reached Fengxiang, military commissioner Zhu Hongzhao received him in the bedchamber and had wife and children present food vessels, serving with utmost deference.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang, commissioner Zhu Hongzhao welcomed him to his private quarters; wife and children served food with deepest respect.

sentences.zh: 重誨坐中言及：「昨有人讒構，幾不保全，賴聖上保鑒，苟獲全族。」

translations.literal: Seated, Chonghui spoke of how "yesterday someone slandered me and I nearly did not survive; relying on the sacred sovereign's protection I barely preserved my clan."
translations.idiomatic: Over the meal Chonghui said, "Yesterday slander nearly destroyed me; only the Emperor's grace spared my house."

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept.

sentences.zh: 重誨既辭，弘昭遣人具奏：「重誨怨望出惡言，不可令至行營，恐奪石敬瑭兵柄。」

translations.literal: After Chonghui took leave, Hongzhao sent men to memorialize: "Chonghui harbors resentment and spoke evil words; he must not be allowed to reach the camp, lest he seize Shi Jingtang's command."
translations.idiomatic: After he left, Hongzhao reported, "Chonghui spoke bitterly in resentment; keep him from the front lest he steal Shi's command."

sentences.zh: 而宣徽使孟漢瓊自西回，亦奏重誨過惡。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Xuanhui commissioner Meng Hanqiong, returning from the west, also memorialized Chonghui's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui commissioner Meng Hanqiong, back from the west, also denounced Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 重誨已至三泉，復令歸闕。

translations.literal: Chonghui had already reached Sanquan when he was ordered to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui had reached Sanquan when orders recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 再過鳳翔，朱弘昭拒而不納，重誨懼，急騎奔程，未至京師，製授河中帥。

translations.literal: Passing Fengxiang again, Zhu Hongzhao refused entry; Chonghui was afraid, spurred his horse on the road, and before reaching the capital was appointed Hedong commander by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao shut him out; in fear he raced on, and before the capital an edict made him Hedong commander.

sentences.zh: 既至鎮，心不自安，遂請致仕。

translations.literal: Once at his post he was ill at ease in mind and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he could not rest easy and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 製初下，其子崇讚、崇緒走歸河中。

translations.literal: When the edict first came down, his sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict issued, sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to him at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 二子初至，重誨駭然曰：「渠安得來？」

translations.literal: When the two sons first arrived, Chonghui said in alarm, "How could they come?"
translations.idiomatic: At their arrival Chonghui cried, "How did they get here?"

sentences.zh: 家人欲問故，重誨曰：「吾知之矣，此非渠意，是他人教來。

translations.literal: The household wished to ask the reason; Chonghui said, "I know already—this is not their wish; others taught them to come.
translations.idiomatic: His family asked why; he said, "I know—they did not choose this; someone sent them.

sentences.zh: 吾但以一死報國家，餘復何言！」

translations.literal: I will repay the state with death alone—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: I owe the state only my death—nothing more to say!"

sentences.zh: 翌日，中使至，見重誨，號泣久之。

translations.literal: The next day an imperial messenger came; seeing Chonghui, he wept a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Next day an imperial messenger came and wept long at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 重誨曰：「公但言其故，勿過相湣。」

translations.literal: Chonghui said, "Sir, speak only the reason—do not pity me overmuch."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui said, "Speak your errand—do not pity me so."

sentences.zh: 中使曰：「人言令公據城異志矣！」

translations.literal: The messenger said, "People say my lord holds the city with alien intent!"
translations.idiomatic: The messenger said, "They say you hold the city in rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 重誨曰：「吾一死未塞責，已負君親，安敢輒懷異志，遽勞朝廷興師，增聖上宵旰，則仆之罪更萬萬矣！」

translations.literal: Chonghui said, "My death alone does not discharge my duty—I have already failed lord and kin; how dare I harbor alien intent, hastily to trouble the court with troops and add to the sacred sovereign's sleepless nights—then my guilt would be ten thousandfold greater!"
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui said, "One death cannot answer my debt—I have failed emperor and kin; how dare I rebel and trouble the court and your sleepless nights—my guilt would only multiply!"

sentences.zh: 時遣翟光鄴使河中，如察重誨有異志，則誅之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhai Guangye was sent to Hedong, as if to investigate whether Chonghui had alien intent, then execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Guangye was dispatched to Hedong to probe rebellion and kill him if guilt were found.

sentences.zh: 既至，李從璋自率甲士圍其第，仍拜重誨於其庭，重誨下階迎拜曰：「太傅過禮。」

translations.literal: When he arrived, Li Congzhang himself led armored soldiers to surround the residence, yet bowed to Chonghui in the courtyard; Chonghui came down the steps to return the bow and said, "Grand Mentor exceeds propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Li Congzhang surrounded the house with troops yet bowed in the courtyard; Chonghui descended to return the bow, saying, "Grand Mentor, too much honor."

sentences.zh: 俯首方拜，從璋以楇擊其首，其妻驚走抱之，曰：「令公死亦不遲，太傅何遽如此！」

translations.literal: As he bowed his head, Congzhang struck it with a mace; his wife ran in alarm to embrace him and said, "My lord's death is not yet late—Grand Mentor, why so hasty!"
translations.idiomatic: Mid-bow Congzhang smashed his head with a mace; his wife rushed to shield him crying, "Lord An need not die yet—Grand Mentor, why such haste!"

sentences.zh: 並擊重誨妻首碎，並剝其衣服，夫妻裸形踣於廊下，血流盈庭。

translations.literal: He struck Chonghui's wife's head as well until it shattered, stripped their clothes, and husband and wife lay naked collapsed in the corridor, blood filling the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered her skull too, stripped them both, and left husband and wife naked in the hall, blood flooding the court.

sentences.zh: 翌日，副使判官白從璋，願以衣服覆其屍，堅請方許。

translations.literal: The next day the deputy commissioner and judge reported to Congzhang, begging to cover the corpses with clothing; only after earnest pleading was it granted.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the deputy asked leave to clothe the bodies; only after urgent pleas was it allowed.

sentences.zh: 及從璋疏重誨家財不及數千緡，議者以重誨有經綸社稷之大功，然誌大才短，不能回避權寵，親禮士大夫，求周身輔國之遠圖，而悉自恣胸襟，果貽顛覆。

translations.literal: When Congzhang inventoried Chonghui's household goods they did not reach several thousand strings; observers said Chonghui had great merit in ordering the altars of state, yet his ambition exceeded his talent, he could not avoid the favor of power, personally honored scholar-officials, sought far-reaching plans to preserve himself and assist the state, yet indulged his own breast entirely, and so met overturn in the end.
translations.idiomatic: His estate proved worth only a few thousand strings; critics said he had saved the dynasty yet aimed too high, clung to power, failed to court the literati or plan for safety, indulged his pride, and was ruined.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：初，知祥將據蜀也，且上表乞般家屬。

translations.literal: (《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: At first, when Zhixiang was about to hold Shu, he also submitted a memorial begging to move his household.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Meng Zhixiang was seizing Shu he asked to move his family.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使安重誨用事，拒其請，知祥曰：「吾知之矣。」

translations.literal: At the time Privy Council commissioner An Chonghui held power and refused the request; Zhixiang said, "I understand already."
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council commissioner An Chonghui ruled and refused; Zhixiang said, "I see."

sentences.zh: 因使密以金百兩為賂，重誨喜而為敷奏，詔許之。

translations.literal: He therefore secretly sent a bribe of a hundred taels of gold; Chonghui was pleased and memorialized on his behalf; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent a hundred taels of gold; Chonghui, pleased, memorialized for him and won permission.

sentences.zh: 及家屬至，知祥對僚吏笑曰：「天下聞知樞密，將謂天地間未有此，誰知隻銷此百金耶，亦不足畏也。」

translations.literal: When the household arrived, Zhixiang said to his staff with a laugh, "All under heaven hear of the Privy Council and suppose nothing like it exists between heaven and earth—who knew it is dispelled by this hundred taels of gold? It is also not to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: When his kin arrived he laughed to his officers, "The world fears the Privy Council as unmatched—yet a hundred taels of gold buys it off; nothing to dread."

sentences.zh: 遂守險拒命。

translations.literal: He then held the passes and defied orders.
translations.idiomatic: He then held the mountains and refused obedience.

sentences.zh: 《五代史闕文》：明宗令翟光鄴、李從璋誅重誨於河中私第，從璋奮楇擊重誨於地，重誨曰：「某死無恨，但恨不與官家誅得潞王，他日必為朝廷之患。」

translations.literal: (《Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties》: Mingzong ordered Zhai Guangye and Li Congzhang to execute Chonghui at his private residence in Hedong; Congzhang struck Chonghui to the ground with a mace; Chonghui said, "A certain death holds no regret—only I regret not helping the Son of Heaven execute the Prince of Lu; he will surely become the court's calamity in days to come."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties》: Mingzong ordered Zhai Guangye and Li Congzhang to kill Chonghui at his Hedong mansion; Congzhang felled him with a mace; Chonghui said, "I die without regret—only that I did not help the Emperor kill the Prince of Lu; he will plague the court hereafter."

sentences.zh: 言終而絕。

translations.literal: When the words ended he expired.
translations.idiomatic: He died as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：《明宗實錄》是清泰帝朝修撰，潞王即清泰帝也。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: the 《Veritable Records of Mingzong》 was compiled in the Qingtai emperor's reign; the Prince of Lu is the Qingtai emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I note: the 《Veritable Records of Mingzong》 was edited under Emperor Qingtai; the Prince of Lu is Qingtai.

sentences.zh: 史臣避諱，不敢直書。

translations.literal: The historiographer avoided taboo and dared not write directly.
translations.idiomatic: The historians evaded taboo and would not name him plainly.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，重誨之志節泯矣！）〉

translations.literal: Alas, Chonghui's integrity of purpose is extinguished!)〉
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Chonghui's loyal resolve is lost to the record!)〉

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭，太原人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖玟，父叔宗，皆為本府牙將。

translations.literal: Ancestor Min, father Shuzong—both were junior officers of the native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Min and father Shuzong were both staff officers of the Taiyuan command.

sentences.zh: 弘昭事明宗，在藩方為典客。

translations.literal: Hongzhao served Mingzong; in the frontier post he was guest-reception officer.
translations.idiomatic: He served Mingzong as guest-reception officer in the prince's domain.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，為文思使，曆東川副使，二年餘，除左衛大將軍，充內客省使。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng year 1 he was Literary Thought commissioner; he passed through Eastern Chuan deputy commissioner for more than two years, then was made Left Guard senior general and Inner Guest Service commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng 1 he became Literary Thought commissioner; after two years as Eastern Chuan deputy he was Left Guard senior general and Inner Guest Service commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: In year 3 he was transferred Southern Xuanhui commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 he became Southern Xuanhui commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明宗親祀南郊，弘昭為大內留守，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Mingzong personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, Hongzhao was grand inner custodian and was given acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong's southern suburban sacrifice Hongzhao was grand inner custodian and made acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 出鎮鳳翔，會朝廷命石敬塘帥師伐蜀，久未成功，安重誨自請西行。

translations.literal: He went out to hold Fengxiang; the court appointed Shi Jingtang to command troops against Shu; long without success, An Chonghui asked to go west himself.
translations.idiomatic: He took Fengxiang; Shi Jingtang's Shu campaign stalled; An Chonghui volunteered to go west.

sentences.zh: 至鳳翔，弘昭迎謁馬首，請館於府署，妻子羅拜，捧卮為壽。

translations.literal: Reaching Fengxiang, Hongzhao met him at his horse's head and asked him to lodge at the commissioner's residence; wife and children kowtowed, raised cups to wish long life.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang Hongzhao met him on the road, lodged him at his mansion, and had wife and children bow and toast his health.

sentences.zh: 弘昭密遣人謂敬瑭曰：「安公親來勞軍，觀其舉措孟浪，儻令得至，恐士心迎合，則不戰而自潰也。

translations.literal: Hongzhao secretly sent word to Jingtang: "Lord An has come in person to comfort the army; observing his conduct he is rash; if he is allowed to arrive, I fear the soldiers' hearts will align with him and the army will collapse without battle.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told Jingtang, "Lord An comes to oversee the army; he acts rashly—if he reaches camp the men may rally to him and you will collapse without fighting.

sentences.zh: 可速拒之，必不敢前，則師徒萬全也。」

translations.literal: Quickly refuse him—he will surely not advance, and then master and troops will be wholly secure."
translations.idiomatic: Turn him back at once—he will not dare advance, and all will be safe."

sentences.zh: 敬瑭聞其言大懼，即日燒營遁還。

translations.literal: Jingtang, hearing the words, was greatly afraid and that day burned camp and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang, terrified, burned camp and retreated the same day.

sentences.zh: 重誨聞之，不敢西行，因返旆東還。

translations.literal: Chonghui, hearing of it, did not dare go west and therefore turned his banners east.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui, hearing this, dared not go west and turned back east.

sentences.zh: 復過鳳翔，弘昭拒而不納。

translations.literal: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao refused entry.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao shut him out.

sentences.zh: 及重誨得罪，其年弘昭入朝，授左武衛上將軍，充宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: When Chonghui fell from grace, that year Hongzhao entered court and was made Left Martial Guard senior general and Southern Xuanhui commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghui fell, Hongzhao came to court as Left Martial Guard senior general and Southern Xuanhui commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長興三年十二月，代康義誠為襄州節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Changxing year 3 he replaced Kang Yicheng as Xiangzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Changxing 3, month 12, he replaced Kang Yicheng at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，秦王從榮為元帥，屢宣惡言，執政大臣皆懼，謀出避之。

translations.literal: In year 4 Prince of Qin Congrong was marshal; he repeatedly proclaimed evil words; the chief ministers all feared and plotted to leave and avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4 the Prince of Qin Congrong was marshal and spoke threats; ministers feared and sought posts away from court.

sentences.zh: 樞密使范延光、趙延壽日夕更見，涕泣求去，明宗怒而不許。

translations.literal: Privy Council commissioners Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou saw the emperor morning and evening in turn, weeping and begging to leave; Mingzong was angry and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou wept daily for release; Mingzong refused in anger.

sentences.zh: 延壽使其妻興平公主入言於中，延光亦因孟漢瓊、王淑妃進說，故皆得免。

translations.literal: Yanshou had his wife Princess of Xingping speak within the palace; Yanguang also advanced persuasion through Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang—thus both were released.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou's wife the Princess of Xingping pleaded within; Yanguang used Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang—both won leave.

sentences.zh: 未幾，趙延壽出鎮汴州，召弘昭於襄陽，代為樞密使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao Yanshou went out to hold Bianzhou; Hongzhao was summoned from Xiangyang to replace him as Privy Council commissioner and was given co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao Yanshou went to Bian; Hongzhao was recalled from Xiangyang as Privy Council commissioner with co-chief councilor rank.

sentences.zh: 十月，范延光出鎮常山，以三司使馮贇與弘昭對掌樞務，與康義誠、孟漢瓊同謀以殺秦王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Fan Yanguang went out to hold Changshan; Revenue commissioner Feng Yun and Hongzhao jointly held Privy affairs, and with Kang Yicheng and Meng Hanqiong conspired to kill the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Month 10 Fan Yanguang went to Changshan; Feng Yun shared the Privy Council with Hongzhao; they joined Kang Yicheng and Meng Hanqiong to plot the Prince of Qin's death.

sentences.zh: 閔帝即位，弘昭以為由己得立，故於庶事高下在心，及赦後覃恩，弘昭首自平章事超加中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended, Hongzhao thought he had been enthroned through himself and therefore in common affairs high and low rested in his heart; after the amnesty and broad grace, Hongzhao was first to leap from co-chief councilor to chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min's accession Hongzhao credited to himself; he dictated policy; after the general amnesty he jumped from co-chief councilor to chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 素猜忌潞王，致其釁隙，以致禍敗。

translations.literal: He always suspected the Prince of Lu and provoked their rift, bringing calamity and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He always distrusted the Prince of Lu, widened the breach, and brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 潞王至陝，閔帝懼，欲奔，馳手詔弘昭圖之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu reached Shan, Emperor Min was afraid and wished to flee; he sent a hand edict by express to Hongzhao to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Prince of Lu's arrival in Shan, Emperor Min panicked and meant to flee; he sent an urgent hand edict to Hongzhao to act.

sentences.zh: 時將軍穆延輝在弘昭第，曰：「急召，罪我也，其如之何？

translations.literal: At the time General Mu Yanhui was at Hongzhao's residence and said, "Urgent summons—the guilt is mine; what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: General Mu Yanhui was at his house and said, "They summon in haste—the blame is mine; what now?

sentences.zh: 吾兒婦，君之女也，可速迎歸，無令受禍。」

translations.literal: My son's wife is your daughter—quickly welcome her back, lest she suffer calamity."
translations.idiomatic: My daughter is your son's wife—fetch her at once lest she be harmed."

sentences.zh: 中使繼至，弘昭援劍大哭，至後庭欲自裁，家人力止之。

translations.literal: Imperial messengers came in succession; Hongzhao drew his sword and wept greatly, went to the rear court intending to kill himself, and the household forcibly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers followed; Hongzhao drew his sword, wept, and went to the rear court to die; his family restrained him.

sentences.zh: 使促之急，弘昭曰：「窮至此耶！」

translations.literal: The messenger pressed urgently; Hongzhao said, "Reduced to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Pressed hard, Hongzhao cried, "Brought to this pass!"

sentences.zh: 乃自投於井。

translations.literal: He thereupon threw himself into a well.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into a well.

sentences.zh: 安從進既殺馮贇，斷弘昭首，俱傳於陝州。

translations.literal: An Congjin, having killed Feng Yun, severed Hongzhao's head; both were sent in relay to Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin killed Feng Yun, took Hongzhao's head, and both were rushed to Shan.

sentences.zh: 及漢高祖即位，贈尚書令。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Later Han ascended, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Gaozu posthumously made him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 朱洪實，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongshi—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongshi's origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 以武勇累曆軍校，長興中，為馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: By martial valor he rose through military ranks; in Changxing he was Horse Army commander.
translations.idiomatic: A career built on valor brought him to Horse Army commander in the Changxing era.

sentences.zh: 秦王為元帥，以洪實驍果，尤寵待之，歲時曲遺，頗厚於諸將。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin was marshal, Hongshi's boldness won special favor; seasonal gifts exceeded those of other generals.
translations.idiomatic: As marshal the Prince of Qin favored his daring; seasonal gifts outdid other commanders.

sentences.zh: 及朱弘昭為樞密使，勢焰尤甚，洪實以宗兄事之，意頗相協。

translations.literal: When Zhu Hongzhao was Privy Council commissioner his power blazed highest; Hongshi treated him as a clan elder and their minds largely aligned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Privy Council commissioner Hongzhao's peak power, Hongshi treated him as kin and they largely agreed.

sentences.zh: 弘昭將殺秦王，以謀告之，洪實不以為辭。

translations.literal: When Hongzhao was about to kill the Prince of Qin he told Hongshi the plot; Hongshi did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao told him of the plot to kill the Prince of Qin; Hongshi raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 時康義誠以其子事於秦府，故恒持兩端。

translations.literal: At the time Kang Yicheng had his son serve the Prince of Qin's household, so he always held to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng's son served the Qin mansion, so he straddled both camps.

sentences.zh: 及秦王兵扣端門，洪實為孟漢瓊所使，率先領騎軍自左掖門出逐秦王，自是義誠陰銜之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin's troops knocked at the Duan Gate, Hongshi was sent by Meng Hanqiong and led the cavalry first from the Left Flank Gate to drive off the prince; from this Yicheng secretly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on the Duan Gate Meng Hanqiong sent Hongshi's cavalry out the Left Flank Gate against the prince; Yicheng thereafter bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 閔帝嗣位，洪實自恃領軍之功，義誠每言，不為之下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, Hongshi relied on his merit in leading the army and would not yield when Yicheng spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min's accession made Hongshi proud of commanding the troops; he would not defer to Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 應順元年三月辛酉，義誠將出征，閔帝幸左藏庫，親給軍士錢帛。

translations.literal: In the third month of Yingshun year 1, on xinyou, Yicheng was about to campaign; Emperor Min visited the Left Treasury and personally gave soldiers cash and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshun 1, third month, day xinyou: Yicheng marched; the emperor visited the Left Treasury to pay the troops in person.

sentences.zh: 是時，義誠與洪實同於庫中麵論用兵利害，

translations.literal: At that time Yicheng and Hongshi were together in the treasury debating the pros and cons of using troops,
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng and Hongshi argued strategy face to face in the treasury,

sentences.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：洪實見軍士無鬥志，而義誠盡將以西，疑其二心。）〉

translations.literal: (《Ouyang History》 says: Hongshi saw the soldiers lacked fighting spirit, while Yicheng was sending them all west, and suspected divided loyalty.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Ouyang History》: Hongshi saw no fighting spirit in the men while Yicheng marched them all west and suspected treachery.)〉

sentences.zh: 洪實言：「出軍討逆，累發兵師，今聞小衄，無一人一騎來者。

translations.literal: Hongshi said, "Campaigning against rebels, we have repeatedly sent armies; now we hear a small setback and not one man or horse has come back.
translations.idiomatic: Hongshi said, "We have sent army after army against the rebels; now at a small defeat not a rider returns.

sentences.zh: 不如以禁軍據門自固，彼安敢徑來，然後徐圖進取，全策也。」

translations.literal: Better to hold the Forbidden Army at the gates and secure ourselves—they would not dare come straight in; then we may slowly plan advance and retreat—the full strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the palace guards at the gates—they will not dare charge in; then plan our next move—that is the whole strategy."

sentences.zh: 義誠怒曰：「若如此言，洪實反也。」

translations.literal: Yicheng said in anger, "If such words, Hongshi rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng snapped, "Say that and you are the rebel."

sentences.zh: 洪實曰：「公自反，誰反！」

translations.literal: Hongshi said, "You yourself rebel—who rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongshi shouted, "You are the rebel—not I!"

sentences.zh: 其聲漸厲。

translations.literal: Their voices grew ever sharper.
translations.idiomatic: Their voices rose louder.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，召而訊之，洪實猶理前謀，又曰：「義誠言臣圖反，據發兵計，義誠反必矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard, summoned and questioned them; Hongshi still argued his former plan and also said, "Yicheng says I plot rebellion; judging by his troop deployments, Yicheng surely rebels."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned them; Hongshi pressed his plan and said, "Yicheng accuses me—by his deployments he is the rebel."

sentences.zh: 閔帝不能明辨，遂命誅洪實。

translations.literal: Emperor Min could not clearly distinguish; he thereupon ordered Hongshi executed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min could not judge; he ordered Hongshi killed.

sentences.zh: 既而義誠果以禁軍迎降潞王，故洪實之死，後人皆以為冤。

translations.literal: Afterward Yicheng indeed used the Forbidden Army to welcome the Prince of Lu in surrender; therefore Hongshi's death—later men all regarded it as wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng soon surrendered the guards to the Prince of Lu; posterity called Hongshi's death a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 康義誠，字信臣，代北三部落人也。

translations.literal: Kang Yicheng, styled Xinchen, was a man of the three tribal groups of northern Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng, style Xinchen, came from the three northern tribal groups.

sentences.zh: 少以騎射事武皇，從莊宗入魏博，補突騎使，累遷本軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth he served the Martial Emperor with mounted archery; following Zhuangzong into Weibo he was made Swift Cavalry officer and rose to commander of the native army.
translations.idiomatic: Young he rode for the Martial Emperor; entering Weibo with Zhuangzong he became a Swift Cavalry officer and rose to command the household guard.

sentences.zh: 同光末，從明宗討鄴城，軍亂，迫明宗為主，明宗不然。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang he followed Mingzong to campaign at Ye city; the army mutinied and forced Mingzong to be ruler; Mingzong did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongguang's end he followed Mingzong against Ye; mutineers pressed Mingzong to rule and he refused.

sentences.zh: 義誠進曰：「主上不慮社稷阽危，不思戰士勞苦，荒耽禽色，溺於酒樂。

translations.literal: Yicheng advanced and said, "The sovereign above does not consider the altars in peril, does not think of the soldiers' toil, indulges in birds and beasts, and drowns in wine and music.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng urged, "The throne ignores peril and the soldiers' pain, drowning in sport and wine.

sentences.zh: 今從眾則有歸，守節則將死。」

translations.literal: Now if we follow the multitude there is return; if we hold to integrity we will die."
translations.idiomatic: Follow the crowd and we live; hold to loyalty and we die."

sentences.zh: 明宗納其言，由是委之心膂。

translations.literal: Mingzong accepted his words; from this he entrusted him with his innermost counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong took his counsel and trusted him with his inmost thoughts.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，加檢校司空，領富州刺史，總突騎如故。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was given acting Minister of Works, held Fuzhou, and still commanded the Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong's accession he became acting Minister of Works, governed Fu, and kept the Swift Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋轉捧聖都指揮使，鎮邠州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to commander of the Sacred Guard and military commissioner of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded the Sacred Guard and held Bin.

sentences.zh: 明宗幸汴，平朱守殷，改侍衛馬軍都指揮使，領江西節度使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong visited Bian and pacified Zhu Shouyin, he was made Palace Guard Horse Army commander and Jiangxi military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian he pacified Zhu Shouyin and became Horse Army commander and Jiangxi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 車駕歸洛，授侍衛馬步軍都指揮使、河陽節度使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang he was made Palace Guard Horse and Foot commander and Heyang military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Luoyang he held Horse and Foot command and Heyang.

sentences.zh: 長興末，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing he was given co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Late Changxing he became co-chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》云：長興中，侍衛使康義誠，嘗軍中差人於大宅充院子，亦曾小有笞責。

translations.literal: (《Idle Talk from the Jade Hall》 says: In Changxing, Palace Guard commissioner Kang Yicheng once detailed a man from a great mansion as courtyard servant and had also lightly flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Idle Talk from the Jade Hall》: Changxing-era commissioner Kang Yicheng once took a man from a great house as yard servant and had him lightly beaten.

sentences.zh: 忽一日，憐其老而詰其姓氏，則曰：「姓康。」

translations.literal: Suddenly one day, pitying his age, he questioned his surname; he said, "The surname is Kang."
translations.idiomatic: One day pitying his age he asked his name: "Kang."

sentences.zh: 別詰其鄉土、親族、息嗣，方知是父，遂相持而泣，聞者莫不驚異。）〉

translations.literal: Questioning further his native place, kin, and offspring, he then knew it was his father; they thereupon embraced and wept; hearers were all startled.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Further questions on home, kin, and children revealed his father; they embraced and wept; all who heard were astonished.)〉

sentences.zh: 長興末，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing he was given co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Late Changxing he became co-chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 秦王為天下兵馬元帥，氣焰熏灼，大臣皆懼，求為外任。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin was marshal of all armies under heaven; his arrogance blazed hot; the chief ministers all feared and sought posts away from court.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin became commander of all armies; his arrogance blazed; ministers feared him and sought posts away from court.

sentences.zh: 義誠以明宗委遇，無以解退，乃令其子以弓馬事秦王以自結。

translations.literal: Yicheng, owing to Mingzong's favor, had no way to resign; he therefore had his son serve the Prince of Qin in archery and horsemanship to curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by Mingzong, Yicheng could not resign; he had his son serve the Prince of Qin in archery and horsemanship to win favor.

sentences.zh: 明宗不豫，秦王諷義誠為助，義誠曲意承奉，亦非真誠。

translations.literal: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Qin urged Yicheng to help; Yicheng bent to flatter him, yet it was not sincere.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Qin urged Yicheng to aid him; Yicheng flattered him insincerely.

sentences.zh: 及朱弘昭、馮贇等懼禍，謀於義誠，但云：「仆為將校，不敢預議，但相公所使耳。」

translations.literal: When Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and the rest feared calamity and plotted with Yicheng, he only said, "I am a military officer; I dare not join deliberations—I do only as the chief councilor commands."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and the rest feared disaster and plotted with Yicheng, he only said, "I am a military officer; I dare not take part in counsel—I do only as the chief councilor orders."

sentences.zh: 及秦王既誅，明宗宴駕，閔帝即位，加檢校太尉、兼侍中，判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Qin was executed, Mingzong died, and Emperor Min ascended; Yicheng was given acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant, and directed the Six Armies and all guards.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Qin was killed, Mingzong died, and Emperor Min took the throne; Yicheng was made acting Grand Commandant and Palace Attendant and put in charge of the Six Armies and all guards.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鳳翔變起，西軍不利，義誠懼，乃請行，蓋欲盡率駕下諸軍送降於潞王求免也。

translations.literal: Before long the Fengxiang revolt rose; the western army fared poorly; Yicheng feared and asked to march—likely intending to lead all troops at the emperor's side in surrender to the Prince of Lu to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Fengxiang revolt broke out; the western army fared badly; Yicheng, afraid, asked to march—likely meaning to lead the emperor's troops in surrender to the Prince of Lu to save himself.

sentences.zh: 會與朱洪實議事不葉，洪實因厲聲言義誠苞藏之志，閔帝曖昧，不能明辨，而誅洪實。

translations.literal: He happened to dispute strategy with Zhu Hongshi; Hongshi cried out that Yicheng harbored treacherous intent; Emperor Min, bewildered, could not judge clearly and executed Hongshi.
translations.idiomatic: He disputed strategy with Zhu Hongshi; Hongshi cried that Yicheng harbored treachery; Emperor Min, confused, could not judge and had Hongshi executed.

sentences.zh: 及義誠率軍至新安，諸軍爭先趨陝，解甲迎降，義誠以部下數十人見潞王請罪，潞王雖罪其奸回，未欲行法。

translations.literal: When Yicheng led the army to Xin'an, the troops raced ahead to Shan, laid down arms and welcomed surrender; Yicheng came with several dozen followers to beg pardon of the Prince of Lu; though the prince blamed his treachery, he did not yet wish to punish.
translations.idiomatic: When Yicheng reached Xin'an, the troops raced to Shan, laid down arms, and surrendered; Yicheng came with several dozen men to beg pardon of the Prince of Lu; though the prince blamed his treachery, he did not yet punish him.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年四月，斬於興教門外，夷其族。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Qingtai year 1 he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Qingtai 1 he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 藥彥稠，沙陀三部落人。

translations.literal: Yao Yanchou was a man of the three Shatuo tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanchou came from the three Shatuo tribes.

sentences.zh: 幼以騎射事明宗，累遷至列校。

translations.literal: In youth he served Mingzong with mounted archery and rose through the ranks to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Young he rode for Mingzong and rose to company rank.

sentences.zh: 明宗踐阼，領澄州刺史、河陽馬步都將。

translations.literal: When Mingzong ascended he held Chengzhou and was Heyang Horse and Foot commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong's accession he held Cheng and commanded Heyang horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 從王晏球討王都於定州，平之，領壽州節度使、侍衛步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Following Wang Yanqiu against Wang Du at Dingzhou, when it was pacified he held Shouzhou and was Palace Guard Foot Army deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Yanqiu he pacified Wang Du at Ding and received Shou and Foot Army deputy command.

sentences.zh: 屬河中指揮使楊彥溫作亂，彥稠改侍衛步軍都指揮使，充河中副招討使，將兵討平之。

translations.literal: When Hedong commander Yang Yanwen rebelled, Yanchou was made Foot Army commander and Hedong deputy pacification commissioner and led troops to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanwen's Hedong revolt made him Foot commander and deputy pacifier; he crushed the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 無幾，党項劫回鶻入朝使，詔彥稠屯朔方，就討党項之叛命者，搜索盜賊，盡獲回鶻所貢駝馬、寶玉，擒首領而還。

translations.literal: Before long the Tangut raided the Uighur tribute mission to court; an edict ordered Yanchou to camp at Shuofang and pursue the Tangut rebels, search out bandits, recover all the camels, horses, and gems the Uighurs had presented, and return having captured the chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut raiders struck the Uighur tribute mission; Yanchou camped at Shuofang, hunted rebels and bandits, recovered the tribute camels, horses, and gems, and returned with chiefs captive.

sentences.zh: 尋授邠州節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Binzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was commissioner of Bin.

sentences.zh: 遣會兵製置鹽州，蕃戎逃遁，獲陷蕃士庶千餘人，遣復鄉里。

translations.literal: He was ordered to join forces and establish control at Salt Prefecture; the frontier tribes fled; more than a thousand commoners and soldiers lost to the tribes were recovered and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to secure Salt Prefecture, the tribes fled; over a thousand captives were restored to their homes.

sentences.zh: 受詔與延州節度使，

translations.literal: He received orders with the Yanzhou military commissioner,
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Yanzhou commissioner,

sentences.zh: 〈（案：原本闕二字。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The original text lacks two characters.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Two characters are missing in the original.)〉

sentences.zh: 進攻夏州，累月不克，兵罷歸鎮。

translations.literal: to attack Xiazhou; for many months they could not take it; the army ceased and returned to post.
translations.idiomatic: to attack Xiazhou; months passed without success; the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 閔帝嗣位，與王思同攻鳳翔，為副招討使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, with Wang Sitong he attacked Fengxiang as deputy pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Min he attacked Fengxiang with Wang Sitong as deputy pacifier.

sentences.zh: 禁軍之潰，彥稠欲沿流而遁，為軍士所擒而獻之。

translations.literal: When the Forbidden Army collapsed, Yanchou wished to flee downriver but was seized by soldiers and presented.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace guard broke, Yanchou tried to flee downstream but soldiers seized and handed him over.

sentences.zh: 時末帝已至華州，令拘於獄，誅之。

translations.literal: At the time the Last Emperor had reached Hua; he ordered him imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor was at Hua; he was jailed and killed.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖即位，與王思同並製贈侍中。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Later Han ascended, he and Wang Sitong were both posthumously made Palace Attendant by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Gaozu posthumously made him and Wang Sitong Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 宋令詢，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Song Lingxun—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lingxun's origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 閔帝在藩時，補為客將，知書樂善，動皆由禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min was still in the frontier post, Lingxun was appointed guest officer; he knew books and loved goodness; every movement followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the prince's domain Lingxun served as guest officer, literate and courteous in all he did.

sentences.zh: 長興中，閔帝連典大藩，遷為都押衙，參輔閫政，甚有時譽，閔帝深委之。

translations.literal: In Changxing Emperor Min successively held great frontier posts; Lingxun was promoted chief military adjutant, assisted border government, won timely reputation, and the emperor deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing the prince held great commands; Lingxun became chief adjutant, won repute in border affairs, and earned deep trust.

sentences.zh: 及閔帝嗣位，朱、馮用事，不欲閔帝之舊臣在於左右，乃出為磁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, Zhu and Feng held power and did not wish the emperor's old followers at his side; he was sent out as Cizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At accession Zhu and Feng ruled and ousted old companions; Lingxun was sent to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 閔帝蒙塵於衛，令詢日令人奔問。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min was driven into hardship at Wei, Lingxun had men run daily to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: In exile at Wei Lingxun sent daily runners to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 及聞帝遇害，大慟半日，自經而卒。

translations.literal: When he heard the emperor had been murdered, he grieved greatly half a day and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the murder he mourned half a day and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫代大匠斫者，猶傷其手，況代天子執賞罰之柄者乎！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: One who hews for the master carpenter still injures his hand—how much more one who holds the Son of Heaven's rewards and punishments!
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Even hewing for a master carpenter cuts the hand—how much more wielding imperial punishments!

sentences.zh: 是以古之賢人，當大任、秉大政者，莫不卑以自牧，推之不有，廓自公之道，絕利己之欲，然後能保其身而脫其禍也。

translations.literal: Therefore the worthies of old, when they held great responsibility and wielded great government, all humbled themselves in self-government, pushed away possession, opened the way of public fairness, and cut off selfish desire—only then could they preserve themselves and escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthies in high office humbled themselves, disclaimed ownership, served the public, and shunned private gain—only then did they survive.

sentences.zh: 而重誨何人，安所逃死，古語云：「無為權首，反受其咎。」

translations.literal: Yet what man was Chonghui, and where could he escape death? The old saying runs: "Do not be the head of power—turn and receive its blame."
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man was Chonghui to escape death? As the proverb says, "Do not lead the power—you will bear the blame."

sentences.zh: 重誨之謂歟！

translations.literal: Is this not Chonghui's case!
translations.idiomatic: Does this not fit Chonghui!

sentences.zh: 自弘昭而下，力不能衛社稷，謀不能安國家，相踵而亡，又誰咎也。

translations.literal: From Hongzhao downward, their strength could not defend the altars, their plans could not settle the state—they perished in succession; upon whom else lay the blame?
translations.idiomatic: From Hongzhao on, none could guard the realm or steady the state—they fell one after another; who else was to blame?

sentences.zh: 唯令詢感故君之舊恩，由大慟而自絕，以茲隕命，足以垂名。

translations.literal: Only Lingxun, moved by his old lord's former grace, through great grief cut off his own life; by this death his name may be handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lingxun, honoring old grace, died by his own hand in grief—a name that endures.
